title: Root grant revocation may race a privileged launch
description: The privileged su path checks the root grant, performs lease-state I/O, then starts su. Revocation updates volatile grant state without a shared lock covering that check-and-launch sequence. No concurrent interleaving or command launch after revocation was observed.
claimed_root_cause: RootAccess.execPrivileged does not serialize the grant check and su process start with RootGrant revocation, leaving a possible check-use race.

trace.description: The privileged execution helper performs authorization checks before starting su.
The helper launches the privileged process after the grant and lease checks.

evidence.description: The AI grant is checked before the subsequent maintenance-lease operations.
Outstanding lease state and dispatch evidence are handled between the grant check and process start.
ProcessBuilder starts su after those checks.

blockers: No deterministic concurrent revoke/dispatch interleaving or root-side effect was observed.
The exact timing and RootManager response to revoke during the check-to-launch interval depend on runtime scheduling and device configuration.
The required OS-enforced sandbox and rooted test device are unavailable.

validation_plan.local: On an isolated rooted test device or bounded harness with a fake su executable that records invocation only, synchronize a grant check, revoke, and process-start boundary. Record whether a new privileged launch can start after revocation without running a destructive command.
validation_plan.deployment: Have the owner reproduce with a disposable rooted test profile and no-op fake command, documenting whether revocation is serialized with an already queued privileged call. Do not use real root commands or user data.
